synthesis_rules.description: Only completed extraction consensus values enter the corpus; reviewer drafts never become findings.
Evidence quotes and locations are copied from reviewer extraction records; quote_hash_verified marks quotes whose SHA-256 matches their stored hash.
Field roles: explicit mapping, then built-in preset keys, then PICOC section names, then field-name heuristics. Every binding records its source.

Theme evidence is read from synthesisThemes/{themeId}/evidence. Its extractedDataValueId is matched against the ids buildSourceValueId gives every (study, field) pair of the corpus, never split. Statuses: resolved, resolved_not_reported (kept, never support), unresolved (with a reason). Duplicates within a theme keep the earliest citation. The cited snapshot is kept for audit and never used as the current value; value_drift compares it with the current value on typed fields. Evidence embedded in theme documents is ignored.
One row per researcher synthesis theme; supporting findings are the resolved values the theme cites. Citations of unreported values and unresolved citations are listed apart.
Every select field, and fields mapped to study_design or topic, is a classification dimension.

Reported findings become finding I-nodes; each researcher theme becomes an RA from the reported values it cites to the theme claim. A cited reported finding is the same node as that finding (same finding_id). No CA or PA is generated.
Layer A JSON Schema and Layer B semantic validation run on every graph; an invalid graph is kept and marked invalid, never repaired.
Study quality comes from the QA phase; certainty per claim is never rated automatically.
Studies are grouped by the normalized values of one role.
Mechanism and moderator relationships are co-occurrences within one study.
Studies with the same outcome value and different effect_direction values form an unverified candidate contradiction.
Cells count studies classified under both categories; empty = 0, sparse = 1..threshold.

High: unverified contradictions and empty cells between categories with at least 2 studies each. Medium: other empty cells, single-study claims, claims without high-quality support, sparse cells without high-quality studies. Low: other sparse cells.
